main_extension.result: The selector-distortion theorem does not require the reported true mean to be constant over time for the production V3 family. Each V3 e-value evaluated at the current true weighted average conditional mean is pointwise dominated by a genuine supermartingale built from the actual per-block conditional means. Therefore the same 2*delta/c(K) selected-pair bound extends to running weighted-average targets whenever the target-to-true evidence distortion K is uniformly bounded over reporting times.
component_domination: For channel j, lambda component and block i, let a_ji=1-exp(-lambda*w_ji), score Y_i in [0,1], and conditional mean mu_i=E[Y_i|F_{i-1}]. Convexity of exp(-lambda*w*y) on y in [0,1] gives E[exp(-lambda*w_ji*Y_i)|F_{i-1}] <= 1-a_ji*mu_i.
Hence M_j,lambda,t = product_i exp(-lambda*w_ji*Y_i)/(1-a_ji*mu_i) is a nonnegative supermartingale.

Let theta_j,t = sum_i w_ji*mu_i / sum_i w_ji. The production V3 denominator dmax_j,lambda,t(theta_j,t) is the maximum of product_i(1-a_ji*v_i) over all v_i in [0,1] with the same weighted average theta_j,t. The actual mu-vector is feasible, so dmax >= product_i(1-a_ji*mu_i).

Therefore the V3 component E_j,lambda,t(theta_j,t) <= M_j,lambda,t pathwise. The fixed positive lambda mixture V_j,t is likewise dominated by M_j,t=sum_lambda p_lambda M_j,lambda,t, itself a supermartingale.
main_extension.two_channel_anytime_step: If selected numerical miscoverage at time t implies V1,t+V2,t >= c(K)/delta, then the dominating supermartingales satisfy M1,t+M2,t >= c(K)/delta. Since (M1+M2)/2 is a supermartingale without any cross-channel independence assumption, Ville yields P(any selected-pair miscoverage)<=2*delta/c(K).
main_extension.superseded_scope_guard: The prior validation's fixed-parameter-only caution is superseded for this exact V3 bounded-score denominator family by the domination argument above. The K bound itself must still hold uniformly over the moving true weighted means and all reporting times.

deployable_guard_form.requirement: Predeclare a scientific parameter/domain constraint and predictable-weight class. Before permitting same-history selected numerical reporting, certify a deterministic K_bar such that for every allowed true conditional-mean path and every reporting prefix, the V3 target-to-true component-ratio bounds imply K_t<=K_bar. If K_bar<=5, the exact nine-split selector inherits joint numerical coverage <=delta with no fresh-data reset. If the guard cannot be certified, use fresh-confirm or a precommitted fixed alpha split.
deployable_guard_form.why_posthoc_is_invalid: K depends on the unknown running true means through denominator ratios. Computing K only at an estimated/observed favorable mean after seeing the same reporting data is not a coverage certificate.
deployable_guard_form.short_horizon_numerical_example: For the finite-grid common-mean audit with equal-process weights 1 and planned-exposure weights alternating .25,1, t<=40 and theta grid [0,.05], max K was 4.836142115617586. At n=80, theta=0 the same calculation gives K=23.388270562450145, so a short-horizon numerical success cannot be extrapolated indefinitely.

measurement_validity_updates: Distinguish whether a confidence-sequence construction evaluated at a moving estimand is itself an e-process versus merely pointwise dominated by one. Domination is sufficient for Ville-style crossing control when the error event forces the reported statistic above a fixed boundary.

A same-history selector can be numerically valid without fresh confirmation if selection evidence and true-parameter evidence remain uniformly coupled strongly enough; for the exact nine-grid the sufficient distortion threshold is K<=5.
Do not infer a deployable K guard from monotonicity alone or from one observed parameter value. The guard must be uniform over the declared unknown-parameter domain and predictable weight histories.
Fresh-confirm remains the portable fallback because it does not require the target-to-true evidence coupling condition.
scope_guards: The domination proof uses bounded scores Y_i in [0,1], predictable weights, the exact V3 denominator maximization contract, and the fixed production positive mixture over lambdas.

The proof controls selected upper-bound miscoverage for the two V3 channels under the exact nine-split minimax selector. It is not a theorem for arbitrary confidence families or arbitrary same-history selectors.
A numerical finite-grid K audit is not a continuum/domain certificate. A production guard needs an analytic or machine-verified worst-case optimization over the declared parameter and weight domain.
If weights depend on the current score rather than only past information, the predictable-weight supermartingale premise can fail.
next_proof_target: Turn the K guard into a parameter-domain certificate for the actual dual-channel block contract: optimize the component-ratio K over all feasible per-block conditional means and predictable exposure weights for bounded horizons, not only a common-mean theta grid. If the worst-case exceeds 5, compute the exact error multiplier 2/c(K) and identify the longest horizon/domain for which same-history numerical reporting remains <=delta before switching to fresh-confirm.
